title: Snack Calculator
story: Chilaka runs a snack stall. Each snack costs 5 rupees, and customers tell you how many they want.
goal: Read a number of snacks with input() and print the total cost (5 rupees each).
starter:
# Read how many snacks, then print the total cost (5 rupees each)
snacks = input()
hints: input() always gives you text. What happens if you multiply text by 5?
Turn the text into a whole number with int(...) before doing maths.
socratic: What type of value does input() give back?
What does "3" * 5 do in Python? Try it in your head.
Which function turns text into a whole number?
explain: In one sentence: why did we need int() here?

example.title: Worked example: double a number
example.code:
n = int("21")  # input() gives text, int() makes it a number
print(n * 2)
example.note: input() always returns text. Convert with int() before doing maths.
